title: The L2 Bridge

captures.note: dry — driven to the quoted Ethereum→Base bridge screen (ETH→ETH on Base), not broadcast

_comment: Moving ETH from Ethereum to an L2 (Base). MetaMask merged Bridge INTO Swap — same closed engine, bridge.api.cx.metamask.io/getQuoteStream, now computing a CROSS-CHAIN route (observed: 0.002 ETH → 0.00198 ETH on Base, rate ~0.991, 0.875% MetaMask fee). The convenient bridge stacks NEW trust beyond a same-chain send: (1) MetaMask's closed quote engine picks the route and the bridge provider you can't see; (2) whatever bridge/relayer that route uses becomes a party that can stall or censor the transfer; (3) you enter Base — Coinbase's L2 — whose sequencer now orders your transactions. THE ZERO-OPTION POINT (Yoav, Aug 25): this convenient path is NOT the escape hatch. The self-sovereign way off an L2 is the FORCED L1 EXIT — submitting your withdrawal directly through the L1 rollup contract without the sequencer's cooperation (Base/OP via the portal's forced inclusion; Arbitrum via the delayed inbox). Slow, painful, technical — but operator-independent. Success there is BINARY: either you can load an exit UI from IPFS and force your way out, or you can't. This map draws the convenient path (observed); the forced exit is the missing zero option.

prepend_steps.purpose: One streamed call returns the cross-chain route, which bridge provider carries it, the minimum received, and the 0.875% fee

prepend_steps.failure_note: no quote → no bridge; no second route source in the UI

worst_lie.note: one closed API picks the bridge provider and the minimum-out; a bad route or a bridge that stalls can strand or lose funds mid-transfer

prepend_steps.notes: Same engine as the M4 swap — MetaMask unified Swap + Bridge. The bridge provider it routes through is not shown to the user.

worst_lie.note: the same RPC company now also sees you on the L2 — your activity on both chains links to one IP + address

prepend_steps.notes: Bridging doesn't escape the RPC dependency — it doubles it (mainnet + the L2), under the same company.
